यमदण्ड: Yamadaṇḍa m.: Name of the missile specially related to Yama. [See Daṇḍa, Yāmya astra]
याम्य: Yāmya astra nt.: A missile special to Yama. Described as heavenly (दिव्य) 12. 5. 14, and fierce (घोर) 7. 53. 43; Arjuna had received it from Yama 7. 53. 43; 12. 5. 13-14; Arjuna's collection of missiles (अस्त्रग्राम) included among other missiles, Yāmya astra 5. 166. 32-33; (Bhīṣma, Droṇa and Yudhiṣṭhira also knew it); Droṇa used it agaisnt Yudhiṣṭhira in order to kill him (जिघांसुः) but Yudhiṣṭhira repelled it apparently by using the same missile 7. 132. 29-30; Bhīṣma and Arjuna used it against each other at the time of the cattle-raid 4. 59. 21. [See Yamadaṇḍa]
यक्षयुद्ध: Yakṣayuddha nt.: Name of the 35th पर्वन् of the Bhārata in the list of a hundred sub-पर्वन्स् supposed to have been made by Vyāsa in the Parvasaṃgraha 1. 2. 44, 33, 70. The incident is mentioned while listing the contents of the Āraṇyakaparvan: Drau-padī asked Bhīmasena to get the Mandāra flowers; for these he went to the Gandha-mādana mountain and dared approach the lotus pond; a great war ensued between him and the Rākṣasas and the Yakṣas headed by Maṇibhadra (who guarded the pond) 1. 2. 112-113; alluded to by Dhṛtarāṣṭra in his summary of the events made for Saṃ-jaya 1. 1. 111; related to the अध्यायस् 3. 155-172.
यजुर्वेद: Yajurveda m.: Name of one of the four Vedic Saṃhitās. A. Relationship with Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa: Nārāyaṇa, the greatest among the gods, told the sage Mārkaṇḍeya that the Yajurveda and the other three Vedas arise from him (at the beginning) and enter into him (at the end) (मत्तः प्रादुर्भवन्त्य् एते माम् एव प्रविशन्ति च) 3. 187. 14; Bhagavān (Kṛṣṇa) told Arjuna that in the Yajur-veda and in the other three Vedas the great sages have listed his many names 12. 328. 8-9; he also told Arjuna that he was described in the ritual texts to be the Yajurveda of one hundred and one branches (षट्पञ्चाशतम् अष्टौ च सप्तत्रैंशतम् इत्य् उत । यस्मिञ् शाखा यजुर्वेदे सो ऽहम् आध्वर्यवे स्मृतः) 12. 330. 33. B. Personified: (i) Yajurveda and Itihāsa acted as rear-guards (पृष्ठरक्षौ) of the chariot of Mahādeva (when he got ready to destroy the Tripuras) 8. 24. 81; (2) Yajurveda, along with the other Vedas, was seen by Nārada, waiting on Pitāmaha (Brahmadeva) in his Sabhā 2. 11. 23, 31. [See Yajus]
यजुस्: Yajus nt. (sg. or pl.): Sacrificial prose formula from the Yajurveda; when used in plural it stands also for the Yajurveda; when in plural, it mostly occurs with ऋच्स् and सामन्स्। A. Gift of Āditya to Yājñavalkya: The sage Yājñavalkya told king Janaka that while he was practising the prescribed rite, (although) he was despised (? अवमतेन), he propitiated the god Sun with severe austerity; he then received from Āditya the यजुसेस् (यथार्षेणेह विधिना चरतावम-तेन ह । मयादित्याद् अवाप्तानि यजूंषि मिथिलाधिप ॥ महता तपसा देवस् तपिष्-ठः सेवितो मया) 12. 306. 2-3; when the pleased god Sūrya offered a boon to Yājña-valkya, the latter requested the god to grant him the यजुसेस् which had not been used before (? यजूंषि नोपयुक्तानि क्षिप्रम् इच्छामि वेदितुम्) 12. 306. 4-5; the god agreed to Yājñavalkya's request; Sarasvatī then in the form of speech entered Yājña-valkya's mouth 12. 306. 6-7; the God said that as a result of that, the whole of Veda (i. e. the Yajurveda) together with its latter half and the खिल would be established in him (Yājñavalkya) (प्रतिष्ठास्यति ते वेदः सोत्तरः सखिलो द्विजा) 12. 306. 10 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 12. 318. 10: खिलं परशाखीयं स्वशाख्यायाम् अपेक्षावशात् पठ्यते तत् खिलम् इत्य् उच्यते । … सखिलम् तत्सहितम्॑ सोत्तरं सोपनिषत्कम् । ); Yājñavalkya received fifteen यजुसेस् from Arka (Sūrya) (दश पञ्च च प्राप्तानि यजूंष्य् अर्कान् मयानघ) 12. 306. 21; Sūrya gave the यजुसेस् (to Yājñavalkya) in the east (अत्र (i. e. in the east) दत्तानि सूर्येण यजूंषि) 5. 106. 11 (Nī on Bom. Ed. 5. 108. 11: याज्ञवल्क्यायेति शेषः). B. Relationship with deities: Nārāyaṇa has his abode in the ऋच्स्, the यजुसेस् and the सामन्स् (ऋग्यजुः-सामधामानम्) 12. 47. 27; Bhīṣma while praising Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa said that he was of the nature of a स्तोत्र and, as a bird named Yajus, had metres for its limbs, Trivṛt (स्तोम) for its head, and Ratha-ntara and Bṛhatī sāmans for its eyes (यः सुपर्णो यजुर् नाम छन्दोगात्रस् त्रि-वृच्छिराः । रथन्तरबृहत्यक्षस् तस्मै स्तोत्रात्मने नमः ॥ ) 12. 47. 28; (Nī., however, on Bom. Ed. 12. 47. 44: सु-पर्णः वेदपुरुषःअ यजुर् इति यस्य नाम छन्दांसि गायत्र्यादीनी यस्य गात्राणि हस्-तादीनि । त्रिवृत् त्रिभिर् ऋग्यजुःसामभिर् वर्-तत इति योगाद् यज्ञाः स एव शिरो यस्य । यस्य रथन्तरं बृहच् च वैकल्पिकं साम प्रीतिवाक्यम्); (2) Upamanyu while praising Śiva said that he was Śatarudriya among the यजुसेस् 13. 14. 159. C. यजुस् and sacrifice (real or metaphorical): The sage Taṇḍi while praising Mahādeva said that the Adhvaryu priests give offerings to him in sacrifice with the repetition of यजुस् formulae 13. 16. 48; Trita, fallen in a well, mentally thought of the ऋच्स्, the यजुसेस् and the सामन्स् for offering a Soma sacrifice (ऋचो यजूंषी सामानि मनसा चिन्तयन् मुनिः) 9. 35. 33; the Yakṣa asked Yudhi-ṣṭhira: “which is the one यजुस् suited for sacrifice ?” (किम् एकं यज्ञ्यं यजुः); the reply was: “mind is the (one) यजुस् suitable for sacrifice” (मनो वै यज्ञियं यजुः) 3. 297. 34-35; one who dwells in a forest (वानप्रस्थाश्रमे वसेत् 12. 236. 5) should, till death, give five (offerings) to the प्राणस् in the three fires in himself with the यजुस् formula, (and) eat six (morsels) with-out criticizing (the food) 12. 236. 25 (त्रींस् चैवाग्नीन् यजेत् सम्यग् आत्मन्य् एवात्म-मोक्षणात् (?) । प्राणेभ्यो यजुषा पञ्च षट् प्राश्नीयाद् अकुत्सयन् ॥ Nī., however, on Bom. Ed. 12. 244. 26: ‘हृदयं गार्ह-पत्यो मोनो ऽन्वाहार्यपचन आस्यम् आह-वनीयः’ इति वैश्वानरविद्योक्तप्रकारेण आत्ममोक्षणाद् देहपातावधि आत्मनि देहे एवाग्नीन् यजेत् … यजुष उच्चारणानन्तरम् पञ्च ग्रासान् प्राश्नीयात् षड् वा । अकुत्सयन् अन्नम् अनिन्दन्). D. यजुस् and meat-eating: One who eats meat which is sancti-fied by the यजुस् formula (i. e. sacrificial meat) incurs no sin (यजुषा संस्कृतं मांसम् उपभुञ्जन् न दुष्यति) 13. 148. 17; consecration by the यजुस् formula is extended even to ordinary food which does not involve killing (नात्मार्थं पाचयेद् अन्नं न वृथा घातयेत् पशून् । प्राणी वा यदि वाप्राणी संस्कारं यजुषार्हति) 12. 235. 5 (Nī., however, on Bom. Ed. 12. 243. 6: प्राणी छागादिः अप्राणी अश्वथादिः यजुषा छेदनमन्त्रेणैव क्रत्वर्थम् एव संस्कारम् अर्हति न तु भक्षणमात्रा-र्थम्); according to 12. 186. 13, however, one who has abstained from meat should not eat (even) meat which is sanctified by the यजुस् formula (i. e. should not eat even sacrificial meat) (यजुषा संस्कृतं मांसम् निवृत्तो मांसभक्षणात् । न भक्षयेत्; Nī. on Bom. Ed. 12. 193. 14: यजुषा यजुर्वेदविदाध्वर्युणा मांसम् यज्ञ्यम् अपि निवृत्तो न भक्षयेत्). E. The study of ऋच्स्, यजुसेस् and सामन्स्: One who does not know the ऋच्स्, the यजुसेस् and the सामन्स् is to be considered as a calamity brought about by Prajāpati (अनृग्यजुर् असामा तु प्राजापत्य उपद्रवः) 12. 60. 42 (Commentator Vimalabodha: अनृग्यजुर् असामा ऋग्वेदादिशून्यः प्राजापत्य उप-द्रवः विधातृकृत उपद्रवः उपघातः । एवंविधो ब्राह्मणो निष्फलजन्मेति भावः cited in the footnote to the stanza in the Cr. Ed.; Nī., however, on Bom. Ed. 12. 60. 44: शूद्रेण उपद्रवतीति तत्समीपगामित्वाद् उपद्रवो दासः शूद्रः स वेदहीनो ऽपि प्राजापत्यः प्रजापतिदेवताकः यथाग्नेयो ब्राह्मण ऐन्द्रोः क्षत्रियस् तद्वत्). F. Personified: यजुसेस् in thousands in the bodily form attended the sacrifice of Mahā-deva who had assumed the body of Varuṇas 13. 85. 4. G. Limitations: Hanūmān told Bhīma that in the Kṛta age there were no सामन्स्, यजुसेस् अन्द् ऋच्स् (नासन् कृतयुगे तात … न सामयजुऋग्वर्णाः) 3. 148. 12-13 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 3. 149. 14: त्रयीध-र्मस्य चित्तशुद्ध्यर्थत्वात् तस्याश् च तदानीम् स्वभावसिद्धत्वान् न सामादीन्य् आसन्) [for other information on यजुस् which is common to the ऋच्स्, the यजुसेस् and the सामन्स् see Ṛc above].
यानसन्धि: Yānasandhi m.: Name of the 53rd पर्वन् in the list of a hundred sub-पर्वन्स् of the Bhārata supposed to have been made by Vyāsa in the Parvasaṃgraha 1. 2. 51, 33, 70. Referred to in the listing of the contents of the Udyogaparvan as: where Saṃjaya, in the assembly of the kings, spoke to Dhṛta-rāṣṭra on the identity of Vāsudeva and Arjuna (ऐकात्म्यं वासुदेवस्य प्रोक्तवान् अर्जुनस्य च) 1. 2. 144; the event is also mentioned in the summary made by Dhṛta-rāṣṭra for Saṃjaya 1. 1. 117-118; related to the अध्यायस् 5. 46-69.
यमस्य: Yamasya Putraḥ m.: Name of a planet (Ketu ?). When Karṇa fell, the rivers stood still, the sun, with a turbid hue set, and the planet, the son of Yama, having the colour of blazing sun arose obliquely (ग्रहश् च तिर्यग् ज्वलि-तार्कवर्णो यमस्य पुत्रो ऽभ्युदियाय राजन्) 8. 68. 47 (one Telugu (T2) ms. actually reads केतुः for राजन्; most Bengali mss., few Devanāgarī and one Grantha read सोमस्य पुत्रो i. e. Budha).
यजन: Yajana nt.: Name of a तीर्थ। Situated in the wide region Devikā along the river of the same name; if one bathes at Yajana one does not grieve over death (उप-स्पृश्य न शोचेन् मरणं ततः) 3. 80. 114-115. [See Devikā]
यमुना: Yamunā f.: Name of a river. A. Location: Listed by Saṃjaya among the rivers of the Bhāratavarṣa; its water used by people for drinking 6. 10. 14, 13; in the north (उदीच्यां … यमुना) 3. 88. 1-2; near the mountain Ārcīka 3. 125. 13, 17-18; Gaṅgā flows at some distance from Yāmunā (गङ्गेव यमुनान्तरे) 6. 18. 18; flowing through the mid-country along with Gaṅgā; a big village of Brāhmaṇas, called Parṇaśālā, situated between Gaṅgā and Yamunā and at the foot of the Yāmunagiri (मध्यदेशे … गङ्गायमुनयोर् मध्ये यामुनस्य गिरेर् अधः) 13. 67. 3; flowing near the Kuru-kṣetra 15. 30. 16; the rivers Jalā and Upa-jalā flow by the side of Yamunā 3. 130. 17; at Prayāga, Yamunā meets Gaṅgā 3. 83. 70; the Bāhlīka country is outsides the rivers Gaṅgā, Sarasvatī and Yamunā (गङ्गया च तिरस्कृताः । सरस्वत्या यमुनया) 8. 30. 10-11; the place Vanaprastha situated on Yamunā (स चागम्य वनप्रस्थं यमुनायाम्) 13. 139. 13. B. Descri-ption: Big river (महानदी) 6. 10. 14; purifying the worlds (लोकपावनी) 3. 83. 70; highly purifying (परमपावनी) 15. 30. 16; holy (पुण्या), removing the fear of sin (पापभयापहा), on the banks of which different sacrifices were offered (नानायज्ञ-चिता) and resorted to by royal sages (राजर्षि-गणसेविता) 3. 125. 22; flowing with undecay-ing stream (अक्षयस्रोतस्) 3. 125. 18; flowing with great speed (महावेगा) 3. 88. 2; the current of Gaṅgā and Yamunā after they meet each other is very terrific and produces fearful sound (गङ्गायमुनयोर् वेगं सु-भीमं भीमनिःस्वनम्) 13. 50. 7; flowing to the ocean (समुद्रगा) 3. 88. 2; all the rivers listed by Saṃjaya are said to be mothers of the universe and very strong 6. 10. 35 (for citation see Atikṛṣṇā). C. Characteristic: The region between Gaṅgā and Yamunā is known as the जघन of earth (गङ्गायमु-नयोर् मध्यं पृथिव्या जघनं स्मृतम्) 3. 83. 71 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 3. 85. 75: जघ-नं नाभेर् अधोभागः). D. Holiness: (1) No sooner one bathes at the confluence of Gaṅgā and Yamunā he gets the religious merit that is obtained by studying the four Vedas and by speaking truth (चातुर्वेदे च यत् पुण्यं सत्यवादिषु चैव यत् । स्नात एव तद् आप्नोति) 3. 83. 80; no gift is superior to a bath at the तीर्थ on Gaṅgā and Yamunā (गङ्गायमुनयोस् तीर्थे … उपस्पृश्य दानं नान्यद् विशिस्यते) 13. 26. 34; (2) The river Yamunā is mentioned among those holy places by visiting which the high-souled ones assume heavenly form, put on heavenly gar-lands and, becoming auspicious and rich in holy fragrance, obtain the Goloka (? गवां विंआने 13. 105. 44) 13. 105. 47-48 (for citation see Karatoyinī); (3) Lomaśa in-vokes Yamunā, besides Varuṇa, Yama and Gaṅgā, in the benediction (स्वस्ति) he pro-nounces on Yudhiṣṭhira 3. 140. 13; (4) There are many तीर्थस् on Yamunā like Plakṣāva-taraṇa and Agniśiras 3. 88. 2-3; Prayāga is at the confluence of Gaṅgā and Yamunā 3. 83. 70-71; 3. 85. 13-14. E. Importance: Finds mention in the Daivata-Ṛṣi-Vaṃśa 13. 151. 22, 2. F. Epic events: (1) The sage Parāśara wanted to cross Yamunā; while he was being ferried over by Satyavatī the sage made advances to her 1. 99. 7-8; Kṛṣṇa Dvaipāyana was born to Kālī (Satya-vatī) from Parāśara on an island in Yamunā (यमुनाद्वीपे) 1. 54. 2; 1. 57. 69; (2) Śaṃtanu offered seven great sacrifices (सप्त मुख्यान् महामेधान्) on the river Ya-munā 3. 159. 23; when he once went to a forest along the river Yamunā he saw a fisher-man's girl who plied a ferry on the river 1. 94. 41, 44; (3) After the Rājasūya, Kṛṣṇa stayed back at Indraprastha and, in the com-pany of Arjuna, used to roam on the banks of Yamunā 1. 213. 57; once, as the days were hot, Arjuna suggested to Kṛṣṇa to spend a day on the bank of Yamunā 1. 214. 14; (4) After leaving Gaṅgā and the Kurukṣetra the Pāṇḍavas, in their westward march, went to Yamunā 3. 6. 2; (5) At the confluence of Gaṅgā and Yamunā the Pāṇḍavas bathed and gave gifts to Brāhmaṇas 3. 93. 6; shown by Lomaśa to the Pāṇḍavas 3. 125. 18, 22; (6) The basket containing the newly-born Karṇa went from the river Carmaṇvatī to Yamunā and from there to Gaṅgā 3. 292. 25; (7) Ambā practised extraordinary austerities (तपस् तेपे ऽतिमानुषम्) on the bank of Yamunā for a year 5. 187. 18, 20; at the end she entered fire near Yamunā saying ‘for the death of Bhīṣma’ (उक्त्वा भीष्मवधायेति प्रविवेश हुताशनम् । … यमुनाम् अभितो नदीम्) 5. 188. 18; (8) The army of the Kauravas, gathered for the war, spread out from Hāstinapura to the land adjacent to Yamunā (यमुनान्तरे) 6. 18. 18; (9) Duryodhana, dejected at the death of Jaya-dratha, told Droṇa that he wanted to offer water oblations near Yamunā to those from his side who were killed in the war (तर्पयि-ष्यामि तान् एव जलेन यमुनाम् अनु) 7. 125. 23; (10) Yudhiṣṭhira, wanting to see Dhṛta-rāṣṭra and others, reached Kurukṣetra and crossed the river Yamunā 15. 30. 16; the as-cetics there told Yudhiṣṭhira that Dhṛtarāṣṭra had gone to Yamunā to get flowers and water (पुष्पाणाम् उदकुम्भस्य चार्थे गत इति प्रभो) 15. 31. 6; (11) Balarāma proceeded from the Kārapacanatīrtha to the hermitage of Mitra and Varuṇa on Yamunā 9. 53. 13; (12) Kṛṣṇa practised austerities on Yamunā 3. 125. 18; (13) Kṛṣṇa killed a lordly horse (the demon Keśin) who lived in the forest on Yamunā (हयराजं … यमुना-वनवासिनम्) 7. 10. 3 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 7. 11. 3: हयराजं केशिनम्); (14) Haṃsa and Ḍimbhaka were two excellent warriors of Jarāsandha; when Dimbhaka heard that Haṃsa (really his namesake) was killed, he drowned himself in Yamunā; when Haṃsa knew this he did the same 2. 13. 40, 42. G. Past events: (1) The semen of King Vasu, being carried by a falcon, fell in the water of Yamunā when another falcon attack-ed it 1. 57. 46; (2) Bharata; son of Duḥ-ṣanta, performed many horse sacrifices; he bound thirty horses for gods (according to 3. 88. 7 thirty-five horse sacrifices) on the river Yamunā 12. 29. 41-42; (3) Yayātī wish-ing to perform the स्वयंवर of his daughter went to a hermitage on the confluence of Gaṅgā and Yamunā 5. 118. 1; he offered sacrifices on Yamunā 3. 129. 2; when Yayāti gave his kingdom to Puru he told him (Puru) that he would be the king of the land in the middle of the earth and he would rule over the entire region between Gaṅgā and Yamunā (गङ्गायमुनयोर् म-ध्ये कृत्स्नो ऽयं विषयस् तव । मध्ये पृथिव्यास् त्वं राजा) 1. 82. 5; (4) King Sahadeva offered sacrifices on the bank of Yamunā 3. 125. 23; there is a गाथा sung by Indra, and which was later sung by the twice-born, which said that Sahadeva offered on Yamunā a hundred thousand sacrifices at which he gave a hundred thousand दक्षिणास् 3. 88. 5-6; (5) King Māndhātṛ and king Somaka offered sacrifices on the bank of the river Yamunā 3. 125. 22-23; (6) Ambarīṣa Nābhāga and Prajāpati himself offered sacri-fices on Yamunā 3. 129. 2; (7) In the region between Gaṅgā and Yamunā Haryaśva was killed by the sons of Hehaya in a battle 13. 31. 11; (9) Sage Cyavana entered the waters of the rivers Gaṅgā and Yamunā at their confluence in order to observe a vow of staying in water for twelve years; he checked the current of the two rivers with his head; the two rivers and the rivers which followed them did not cause any pain to the sage but made a प्रदक्षिणा around him (गङ्गा च यमुना चैव सरितश् चानुगास् तयोः । प्रदक्षिणम् ऋषिं चक्रुर् न चैणं पर्यपीडयन् ॥ ); Cyavana slept in waters like a log of wood; when once some fishermen cast their net to catch fish they dragged out Cyavana, along with fish, from the water of the two rivers 13. 50. 6-9, 11-20; (a) Agastya practised austerities on the bank of Yamunā 3. 158. 52; (10) Varuṇa abducted Bhadrā (Uta-thya's wife) from Vanaprastha on Yamunā and took her to his city 13. 139. 13-14; (11) Mārkaṇḍeya saw Yamunā, among other rivers, in the belly of the Bāla (3. 186. 83, i. e. Nārāyaṇa 3. 187. 3) 3. 186. 93. H. Similes: (1) Bhīṣma, when he fell down from the chariot, was covered with arrows as with the stream of Yamunā (स्रोतसा यामु-नेनेव शरौघेण परिप्लुतम्) 7. 3. 3; (2) The two armies of the Kauravas and the Pāñcālas in their confrontation made terrific dash as the two rivers Jāhnavī and Yamunā do in the rainy season when they are full of water 7. 70. 8; 8. 31. 68; (3) King Bṛhadratha appeared between his two wives as the ocean, in bodily form, appears between the rivers Gaṅgā and Yamunā (गङ्गायमुनयोर् मध्ये मूर्तिमान् इव सागरः) 2. 16. 19.
यमुनाद्वीप: Yamunādvīpa: See Yamunā, F. Epic events (1. 54. 2; 1. 57. 69).
ययातिपतन: Yayātipatana nt.: Name of a sacred place. One can reach it from the Kaṇvāśrama; by visiting it one gets the fruit of a horse sacrifice (हयमेध) 3. 80. 67.
यवक्रीतस्य: Yavakrītasya tīrtham nt.: Designation of a तीर्थ। The तीर्थ on the river Bhāgīrathī where Yavakrīta used to go for his purificatory cere-monies is so designated; Indra started to build a bridge there with sand (यवक्रीतस्य यत् तीर्थम् उचितं शौचकर्मणि । भागी-रथ्यां तत्र सेतुं वालुकाभिश् चकार सः) 3. 135. 31.

Yavakrītasya āśramaḥ m.: The her-mitage of Yavakrī(ta). A. Location: It was probably establi-shed by his father Bharadvāja (3. 135. 12-13, 42) near the आश्रम of Raibhya 3. 137. 1. B. Description: Described as holy (पुण्य) and having trees with flowers and fruits at all times (सदापुष्पफल-द्रुम) 3. 139. 24. C. Holiness: One who stayed there could be free of all sins (अत्रोष्य राजशार्दूल सर्वपापैः प्रमोक्ष्यसे) 3. 139. 24. [See Bharadvajāśrama]
याजन: Yājana nt.: Name of a तीर्थ। Situated in the wide region designated as Devikā along the river of the same name; by visiting it and by bathing (उपस्पृश्य) at this तीर्थ one does not grieve over death (न शोचेन् मरणं ततः) 3. 80. 114-115. [See Devikā]
यामुन: Yāmuna1 (giri, adrī, parvata) m.: Name of a mountain related to the river Yamunā. A. Location: In the Madhyadeśa; a big settlement of Brāhmaṇas, known as Parṇa-śālā, was situated at the foot of the Yāmuna mountain and between the rivers Gaṅgā and Yamunā (मध्यदेशे महान् ग्रामो ब्राह्-मणानाम् … । गङ्गायमुनयोर् मध्ये या-मुनस्य गिरेर् अधः ॥ पर्णशालेति विख्या-तः) 13. 67. 3-4; located at some distance from Hāstinapura (यामुनश् चैव पर्व-तः) 5. 19. 28, 30; a place called Viśākhayūpa was on this mountain (तस्मिन् गिरौ) 3. 174. 16. B. Description: King of mountains (अद्रिराज), full of streams (प्रस्रवणोप-पन्न), its pale red peaks covered with snow (हिमोत्तरीयारुणपाण्डुसानु) 3. 174. 16. C. Characteristics: Characterized by a big forest full of boats, various animals and birds and which looked like the forest of Citra-ratha (वराहनानामृगपक्षिजुष्टं महद् वनं चैत्ररथप्रकाशम्) 3. 174. 17; (तस्माद् वनात् चैत्ररथप्रकाशात्) 3. 174. 20. D. Epic events: (1) The Pāṇḍavas, after they met Arjuna, descended from the Himavant and stayed at Viśhākhayūpa on the Yāmuna mountain for a year (the twelfth year) 3. 174. 15-16, 20; (2) The army of the Kauravas, gathered for the war, spread on a wide region extending up to the Yāmuna mountain as it did not have enough space in Hāstinapura (यामुनश् चैव पर्वतः । एष देशः सुविस्तीर्णः … । बभूव कौरवे-याणां बलेन सुसमाकुलः ॥ ) 5. 19. 28, 30-31.

yāmuna2 nt.: Name of a तीर्थ। Located at the source of the river Yamunā; by bathing there one gets the fruit of a horse sacrifice and is glorified in heaven (यमुनाप्रभवं गत्वा उपस्पृश्य च यामुने । अश्वमेधफलं लब्ध्वा स्व-र्गलोके महीयते ॥ ) 3. 82. 39. [See Pla-kṣāvataraṇa]
यायात: Yāyāta nt.: Name of a तीर्थ (related to Yayāti). From the तीर्थ on the river Sarasvatī near the आश्रम of Baka Dālbhya, Balarāma went to the Yāyāta तीर्थ; Yayāti, son of Nahuṣa, offered a sacrifice there for which the river Sarasvatī yielded clarified butter and milk and also fulfilled the desires of the Brāhmaṇas (यत्र यज्ञे ययातेस् तु महा-राज सरस्वती । सर्पिः पयश् च सुस्राव  … ॥ … सरस्वती । प्रसृता प्रददौ कामान् ब्राह्मणानां महात्मनाम् ॥ ) 9. 40. 29-30, 32-33.
योनि: Yoni f.: Name of a तीर्थ। On the river Bhīmā; described as the best place on that river (भीमायाः स्थानम् उत्तमम्) 3. 80. 100; if one bathes there one becomes the son of a goddess (?) and puts on shining कुण्डलस् (देव्याः पुत्रो भवेद् राजंस् तप्तकुण्डलविग्रहः); he also gets the great fruit (फलं … महत्) of gifting a hundred thousand cows 3. 80. 101.
योनिद्वार: Yonidvāra nt.: Name of a तीर्थ। Situated on the mountain Udyant 3. 82. 81; described as famous (विश्रुत); if one visits it one is freed of the sin of misalliance (तत्राभिगम्य मुच्येत पुरुषो योनिसं-करात्) 3. 82. 83.
यवनानां: Yavanānāṃ puram nt.: The city of the Yavanas. Located outside the Bhāratavarṣa; Sahadeva in his expedition to the south of Hāstinapura प्रययौ दक्षिणां दिशम् 2. 28. 1; दक्षिणाभिमुखो ययौ 2. 28. 8) and along the seacoast before the Rājasūya sub-jugated it by just sending his messengers and made the people of the town pay tribute (यवनानां पुरं तथा । दूतैर् एव वशे चक्रे करं चैनान् अदापयत् ॥ ) 2. 28. 49 (The city referred to is possibly Alexandria, See Edgerton's note on the stanza, Cr. Edn. Vol. II. p. 502 and his article in JAOS 58. 262-265).
युगन्धर: Yugandhara nt.: Name of a town. A. Location: In the Āraṭṭa (Bāhlīka) country (आरट्टा नाम बाह्लीका वर्जनीया विपश्चिता) 8. 30. 40, 9, 36. B. Unholy: If one drank milk at Yugandhara one could not go to heaven-this is what a Brāhmaṇa told in the assembly of the Kurus (यद् अन्यो ऽप्य् उक्तवान् सभ्यो ब्राह्मणः कुरु-संसदि । युगन्धरे पयः पीत्वा … कथं स्वर्गं गमिष्यति) 8. 30. 41-42 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 8. 44. 39: युगन्धरे नगरे औष्ट्रादिकम् अपि क्षीरं पीयते, भक्ष्या-भक्ष्यविवेकाभावात् तत्रावश्यम् अभक्ष्य-भक्षणम् आपतत्य् एव (cf. 8. 30. 39)); the town is also mentioned in what a Piśācī told a woman who, with her son(s), came to stay near the river Raupyā; according to the Piśācī one who has eaten curds at Yugandhara was not supposed to stay near Raupyā for more than one night; otherwise some calamity would overtake the person at night (पिशाची यद् अभाषत । युगन्धरे दधि प्राश्य … एकरात्रम् उषित्वेह द्वितीयं यदि वत्स्यसि । एतद् वै ते दिवा वृत्तं रात्रौ वृत्तं अतो ऽन्यथा) 3. 129. 8-10 (according to the प्राञ्चः whose view is cited by Nī. on 3. 129. 9 one was required to undergo a प्रायश्चित्त called प्राजा-पत्य व्रत, prescribed in the Dharma-śāstra, if one ate curds at Yugandhara: अत्र प्राञ्चः । … पिशाची वदति॑त्वया युगन्-धरे पर्वते देशे वा दधिप्राशनं कृतम् । तत्र उष्ट्रीक्षीरं गर्दभ्यादिक्षीरं च दधीक्रियते । … एतत्करणे हि प्रायश्चित्तं धर्मशास्त्रे प्रसिद्धम् । ‘औष्ट्रम् ऐक-शफं क्षीरं सुरातुल्यम्’ इति । ‘संसृज्य संकरैः सार्धं प्राजापत्यं व्रतं चरेत्’ इति; according to अर्वाञ्चः, however, eating curds etc. entitled the person to stay near Raupyā for one night, but not a second; according to these interpreters of the stanza युगन्धर meant जीव and दधिप्राशन meant leading a married life for paying back the threefold debt: युगन्-धरः स्थूलशरीराभिमानि जीवः । … दधि-प्राशनशब्देन धर्मप्रजासंपत्त्यर्थो दारसंयोग उच्यते । … दधिप्राशन-शब्देन लक्षितलक्षणया आनृण्यं ग्राह्यम् । तेन स्वधर्मनिष्ठः प्रजावान् एतत् तीर्थं सेवितुम् अर्हतीति पूर्वपादार्थः । ).

Yugandhara m. (pl.): Name of a Janapada. A. Location: Saṃjaya listed Yugan-dhara among the northern Janapadas (also called Deśas 6. 10. 68) of Bhārata-varṣa (अत ऊर्ध्वं जनपदान् निबोध) 6. 10. 37, 5; (शाल्वा युगन्धराः) 4. 1. 9; also called Rāṣṭra 4. 1. 8; it lay around the Kuru country (परितः कुरून्) 4. 1. 9. B. Description: Pleasing (रम्य) 4. 1. 9; (रमणिय) 4. 1. 8; protected (गुप्त) 4. 1. 8; having ample food (बह्वन्न) 4. 1. 9. C. Epic event: Arjuna suggested Yugan-dhara to Yudhiṣṭhira among those countries (Rāṣṭras or Janapadas) where Pāṇḍavas could stay during their अज्ञातवास (किं तु वासाय राष्ट्राणि कीर्तयिष्यामि कानिचित् ।  … सन्ति रम्या जनपदा … मल्लाः शाल्वा युगन्धराः) 4. 1. 8-9.
यदु: Yadu, Yādava m. (pl.): Name of a people, often identified with Vṛṣṇis so that their accounts get mixed up; some-times mentioned also along with Andhakas and Bhojas. A. Origin: Yādavas were born in the line of Yadu, son of Yayāti (यदोस् तु यादवा जाताः) 1. 80. 26; (यदुश् च … यादवानां कुलकरो … ) 5. 147. 6-7; the lineage of Yadus is traced back to Viva-svant (पुत्रा विवस्वतः सर्वे … तेभ्यो ऽयं कुरुवंशश् च यदूनां भरतस्य च) 1. 1. 41, 44; Other accounts: (1) Baladeva and Kṛṣṇa were born from the two hair-one white and the other black-plucked by Hari and which entered Rohiṇī and Devakī of the lineage of Yadus; (स चापि केशौ हरिर् उद्बबर्ह शुक्लम् एकम् अपरं चापि कृष्णम् । तौ चापि केशौ विशतां यदूनां कुले स्त्रियौ रोहिणीं देवकीं च । तयोर् एको बलदेवो बभूव कृष्णो द्वितीयः) 1. 189. 31; (2) Nārāyaṇa was born on this earth (as Kṛṣṇa) in the house of Yadus and in the lineage of Andhakas and Vṛṣṇis ( … नारायणः … अजायत यदुक्षये । क्षिताव्-अन्धकवृष्णीनां वंशे) 2. 33. 16-17 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 2. 36. 16; यदुक्षये यदुगृहे). B. Glorification of the family of Yadus and of their narrative: Kings born in the lineage of Yadus were incarnations of gods (इति देवासुराणां ते … अंशावतर-णं राजन् … कीर्तितम् ॥ … महात्मानो यदूनां च ये जाता विपुले कुले) 1. 61. 99-100, also cf. 92; the narrative of the family of Yādavas, as also of Pauravas and Bhāratas, is holy, leads to well-being, brings wealth, fame and long life (यादवा-नाम् इमं वंशं … पुण्यं स्वस्त्यय-नं महत् । धन्यं यशस्यम् आयुष्यं … ) 1. 70. 2. C. Description: Of unlimited energy (अमितौजस्) 16. 9. 12; spirited, of true valour, very strong; led by Kṛṣṇa, they all were like Indra and got all enjoyments (कृष्णप्रणीताः सर्व एवेन्द्रकल्पाः । मनस्विनः सत्यपराक्रमाश् च । महा-बला यादवा भोगवन्तः ॥ ) 5. 28. 12 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 5. 28. 12; कृष्णप्रणीताः कृष्णेनल्व नीतिपथं नीताः); their kings were magnanimous (महात्मन्) 1. 61. 100. D. Epic events: (1) Yādavas, Andhakas and Bhojas had abandoned Kaṃsa in the interest of the family; after he was killed by Kṛṣṇa, all his kinsmen lived happily for a hundred years (अन्धका यादवा भोजाः समेताः कंसम् अत्यजन् । … एवं ते ज्ञातयः सर्वे मोदमानाः शतं समाः ॥ ) 2. 55. 6-7; कंसम् एकं परि-त्यज्य कुलार्थे सर्वयादवाः । संभूय सुखम् एधन्ते … अन्धकवृष्णयः ॥ ) 5. 126. 39; (2) Karṇa advised Duryo-dhana to use force against Pāṇḍavas before Kṛṣṇa came with the army of Yādavas to help them (कर्षन् यादववाहिनीम्) 1. 194. 15; (3) The messenger sent by Yudhi-ṣṭhira to Kṛṣṇa reached the country of Yādavas and saw him in Dvārakā (प्राप्य यादवान्) 2. 12. 29; (4) Kṛṣṇa spread the fame and pride of Yādavas by killing Śiśupāla (यशोमानौ वर्धयन् यादवा-नाम्) 5. 22. 26; (5) Pradyumna assured Yādavas that he would destroy the army of Śālva with his arrows 3. 17. 31; 3. 18. 1; (6) Sahadeva recalled that Arjuna had defeated Yādavas who had gathered toge-ther when he abducted Subhadrā; Arjuna had then stayed with the Yadus 3. 79. 27; (यदुसदनं) 8. 26. 63; (7) Bhīma assured Yudhiṣṭhira that Kṛṣṇa with Yādavas would help him to achieve his purpose 3. 173. 16; (8) In the forest, Draupadī and Satyabhāmā told each other interesting stories of those who ruled Kurus and Yadus (कथयाम् आसतुश् चित्राः कथाः कुरुयदुक्षिताम्) 3. 222. 2 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 3. 233. 3 who reads कुरुयदूत्थिताः) explains it as कुरुषु यदुषु च उत्-पन्नाः); (9) Dhṛtarāṣṭra remembered that the Māgadha king with the assis-tance of Karṇa had checked all Kṣatriyas except Kauravas and Yādavas (अरौत्सीत् पार्थिवं क्षत्रम् ऋते कौरवयादयान्) 8. 5. 22; (10) Kuntī felt that nothing would be more painful to her than the fight between Pāṇḍavas, Cedis, Pāñcālas and Yādavas with Bhāratas (i. e. Kauravas) ( … यादवाश् च समागताः । भारतैर् यदि योत्स्यन्ति किं नु दुःखम् अतः परम्) 5. 142. 12; (11) From Upa-plavya, Balarāma along with all Yādavas set out for तीर्थयात्रा to Sarasvatī under the constellation Maitra (मैत्रे नक्षत्र-योगे स्म सहितः सर्वयादवैः) 9. 34. 12; (12) Kṛṣṇa told Gāndhārī that he had already foreseen the destruction of Yādavas brought about by mutual killings (परस्परकृतं नाशम् अतः प्राप्स्यन्ति यादवाः) 11. 25. 45; (13) Younger Yāda-vas took hold of the sacrificial horse of Yudhiṣṭhira and were taking him away when Ugrasena stopped them (यादवानां कुमारकाः) 14. 84. 14; (14) Bhīma and the rest, as well as Kurus and Yādavas, enjoyed listening the stories of Arjuna 14, 89. 11; (15) Yādavas and their wives went to Prabhāsa taking with them ample food and drink and lived there 16. 4. 9; there Sātyaki told Kṛtavarman that Yādavas had not forgotten his killing those who were asleep 16. 4. 9, 17; Kṛṣṇa told Dāruka to go to Kurus and inform Arjuna about the killings of Yadus; he wanted Arjuna to come to Dvārakā hear-ing the news of the death of Yādavas due to the curse of Brāhmaṇas (पार्थाय शं-सस्व वधं यदूनाम्) 16. 5. 2; (श्रुत्वा मृतान् यादवान् ब्रह्मशापात्) 16. 5. 3; Kṛṣṇa told Vasudeva that he was witness to the destruction of Yadus and that he would not be able to bear the sight of the city (Dvārakā) of Yādavas when it was devoid of Yadus (दृष्टं मयेदं निधनं यदूनां … नाहं विना यदुभिर् यादवानां पुरीम् इमां द्रष्टुम् इहाद्य शक्तः) 16. 5. 8; यवन: Yavana m. (pl.): Name of a people. A. Location: Listed by Saṃjaya among the northern Mleccha tribes of Bhāratavarṣa (उत्तराश् चापरे म्लेच्छा जना … । यवनाश् च सकाम्बोजा … म्लेच्छजातयः ॥ ) 6. 10. 64, 5; lived in different parts: (1) the north-west (5. 19. 21), (2) the east (2. 47. 12), (3) outside India in Greece (2. 28. 49). B. Different origins: (1) Yavanas were sons of Turvasu, the son of Yayāti (तुर्वसोर् यवनाः सुताः) 1. 80. 26; (2) Angered Nandinī, cow of Vasiṣṭha, created Yavanas from her urine (मूत्रतश् चासृजच् चापि यवनान् क्रोधमूर्छिता) 1. 165. 35; (3) Originally Kṣatriyas, they became degraded to the status of वृषल due to their disregard of Brāhmaṇas (यवन-काम्बोजास् तास् ताः क्षत्रियजातयः । वृषल-त्वं परिगता ब्राह्मणानाम् अदर्शनात् ॥ ) 13. 33. 19; 13. 35. 18. C. Description and characteristics: Rough (दारुण) 6. 10. 64; fierce and doing cruel deeds (उग्र, क्रूरकर्मन्) 8. 51. 18; very terrible and having fearful eyes (सुघोर, घोरचक्षुस्) 7. 68. 41; especially brave (शूराश् चैव विशेषतः) 8. 30. 80; expert in fighting with fists (नियुद्धकुशल) 12. 102. 5 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 12. 101. 5: नियुद्धं बाहु-युद्धम्; they knew everything correctly (though not expressed in words) (सर्वज्ञ) 8. 30. 80; they knew the मायास् of Asuras (विदन्त्य् असुरमायां ये) 7. 68. 41; they are occasionally characterized as म्लेच्छस् 2. 47. 12; 3. 186. 29-30; 6. 10. 63-64; 7. 95. 12-13; although they lived in countries they led the life of Dasyus (सर्वे विषय-वासिनः । … सर्वे ते दस्युजीविनः) 12. 65. 15. D. Epic events: (1) Mighty king Kampana all alone always terrified Yavanas (सततं कम्पयाम् आस यवनान् एक एव सः) 2. 4. 20; (2) Sahadeva, in his expedition to the south (2. 28. 1; 2. 23. 9) subjugated the town of Yavanas (possibly Alexan-dria) by just sending messengers and made them pay tribute (यवनानां पुरं तथा । दूतैर् एव वशे चक्रे करं चैनान् अदापयत्) 2. 28. 49 (cf. Edgerton's note on the stanza, Cr. Edn. Vol. II, p. 502); Yavanas, led by Bhagadatta, attended the Rājasūya of Yudhiṣṭhira 2. 47. 12; kings of Yavanas acted as servants at the Rājasūya sacrifice (यज्ञे ते परि-वेषकान्) 3. 48. 18, 20, 22; (3) Sudakṣiṇa, a Kāmboja, with an army of Yavanas and Śakas, अक्षौहिणी strong, joined the side of Duryodhana 5. 19. 21; at the instance of Duryodhana, Yavanas and others marched out of Hāstinapura towards Kurukṣetra in the second division (द्वितीये निर्ययुर् बले) 5. 196. 7-8; (4) Before the start of the war Yavanas and others led by Kṛpa stood guard in the north for the Vyūha of the Kauravas (6. 20. 3) (चमूम् उत्तरतो ऽभिपाति) 6. 20. 13; (5) On the second day of the war, Yavanas and others, led by Duḥśāsana, were to protect Bhīṣma (भीष्मम् एवाभिरक्षन्तु) 6. 47. 7, 9; (6) On the sixth day, Yava-nas were among those who were posted at the right wing of the Krauñcavyūha (6. 71. 14) of the Kauravas (दक्षिणं पक्षम् आश्रित्य स्थिता व्यूहस्य) 6. 71. 20; (7) On the eighth day, Trigarta, accompanied by thousands of Yavanas, followed Bṛhad-bala in the Mahāvyūha (6. 83. 9) of Kauravas 6. 83. 10; (8) On the eleventh day, Yavanas and Śakas riding swift horses guarded the extreme end (प्रपक्ष) of the left wing of the Śakaṭavyūha (7. 6. 15) of the Kauravas (सव्यं पार्श्वम् अपाल-यन्) 7. 6. 4-5; that day, Dhṛtarāṣṭra, while recounting Kṛṣṇa's past exploits, mention-ed his victory over Yavanas and their followers (यवनांश् च सहानुगान्) 7. 10. 18; (9) On the twelfth day, Yavanas were posted at the neck (ग्रीवायाम्) of the Suparṇavyūha (7. 19. 4) of the Kaura-vas 7. 19. 7; (10) On the fourteenth day, Arjuna killed hundreds of thousands of Yavanas (शतसहस्रशः) 7. 68. 41, 43; on that day, striking Yavanas holding bows and arrows in their hands and wearing armours, led by Duryodhana faced Sātyaki to fight with him; but Sātyaki was going to kill them all, foot-soldiers and those driving in chariots or riding elephants along with their horses and ele-phants, and break their chariots, (यत्रैते सतनुत्राणाः सुयोधनपुरोगमाः । … शरबाणासनधरा यवनाश् च प्रहारिणः) 7. 95. 11-14; when Sātyaki reached the Yavanas, many of them, quick in action (लघुहस्ताश् च) showered arrows on him; Sātyaki cut off their arrows and missiles; he also cut off their arms and heads; his arrows pierced through their steel armours (शैक्यायसानि वर्माणि) and went through their bodies; dead, they fell down on the ground by hundreds 7. 95. 31-36; Sātyaki killed five, six, seven or even eight (पञ्च षट् सप्त चाष्टौ च) of them at a time with his arrows 7. 95. 37; thus Sātyaki routed (विद्राव्य) the large army of Yavanas and proceeded towards Arjuna 7. 95. 45; 7. 96. 1; at the instance of Duryodhana and led by him Yavanas returned to fight once again with Sātyaki and attacked him (ते पुनः संन्यवर्तन्त … । परां युद्धे मतिं कृत्वा पुत्रस्य तव शासनात् ॥ ) 7. 97. 12-14; (10) On the seventeenth day Yavanas, in chariots and on horse-backs and their footsoldiers, stood at the extreme end of left side of the Bārhaspatyavyūha (8. 31. 26) of Kauravas and, as directed by Karṇa, challenged Arjuna and Kṛṣṇa (वामं पार्श्वम् अपालयन् । … तेषां प्रप-क्षः … शकाश् च यवनैः सह ॥ निदेशात् सूतपुत्रस्य सरथाः साश्वपत्तयः । आह्व-यन्तो ऽर्जुनं तस्थुः केशवं च … ॥ ) 8. 31. 14-16; at the instance of Śakuni, three thousand Yavanas, honoured by the brave, holding शक्तिस्, ऋष्टिस्, and प्रासस् in their hands attacked Bhīma; when beaten and slashed by Bhīma with sword, they raised a loud roar (ताडितानां च सर्वशः । असिभिश् छिद्यमानानाम्) 8. 35. 37; Arjuna attacked the extreme end (of the left side of) the व्यूह (8. 40. 99-100, 110) and fought with Kāmbojas, Yavanas and Śakas who rode horses; they were all smeared with blood (यवनैः … । शोनिताक्तैस् तदा रक्तं सर्वम् आसीद् … ) 8. 40. 108; Kṛṣṇa told Arjuna that no one else but he (Arjuna) could conquer Yavanas and others who had joined hands with Kauravas for the sake of Duryodhana (एते दुर्योधन-स्यार्थे संरब्धाः कुरुभिः सह । न शक्या युधि निर्जेतुं त्वदन्येन परं-तप ॥ ) 8. 51. 18, 20; Yavanas riding horses attacked Arjuna to kill him; Arjuna cut off their arms, holding excellent weapons, and their heads with क्षुर arrows (यव-नाश् च सादिनः । … क्षुरैर् न्यकृन्तंस् त्वरिताः शिरांसि च) 8. 64. 16-17; (11) On the eighteenth day, Kṛpa accompanied by Śakas and Yavanas stood on the right side (दक्षिणे पार्श्वे) of the Sarvato-bhadravyūha (9. 7. 19) of Kauravas 9. 7. 24; (12) On the nineteenth day, in the morning (पूर्वाह्णसमये 9. 1. 14), Saṃ-jaya returned from the camp and while reporting to Dhṛtarāṣṭra about the war mentioned that all Yavanas were killed 9. 1. 26; hearing that, Dhṛtarāṣṭra remem-bered that Yavanas were ready to fight for him unmindful of their death (मदर्-थम् उद्यताः सर्वे प्राणांस् त्यक्त्वा रणे … ) 9. 2. 18. 21. E. Past event: King Māndhātṛ once asked Indra the धर्म of people like Yavanas and how they should be controlled by kings like him (कथं धर्मं चरेयुस् ते … मद्-विधैश् च कथं स्थाप्याः) 12. 65. 13, 15; Indra thereupon told him the duties of all Dasyus (the term included Yavanas) 12. 65. 17-22. F. Future event: Yavanas listed among the Mleccha kings who in the Kali age would rule the earth the wrong way, would be sinful, and given to telling lies (कलौ युगे … बहवो म्लेच्छ-राजानः प्रिथिव्यां … मिथ्यानुशासिनः पापा मृषावादपरायणाः ॥ … यवनाश् च नराधिपाः) 3. 186. 27, 29-30. G. Some kings characterized simply as Yavana or as king of Yavanas: (1) यवन: Kaśerumant 3. 13. 29; (2) यवनाधिप: Naraka and Mura 2. 13. 13; (3) यवनाधिपति: Not named 2. 4. 22. [See Mleccha]
यायावर: Yāyāvara m. (pl.): Name of a group (गण) of ऋषिस्। A. Qualities: Of strict vows (सं-शितव्रत) 1. 13. 14; 1. 41. 16; they practised severe austerities and were expert knowers of धर्म for they were the direct seers of धर्म, hence characterized as ऋषिस् ( … प्रत्यक्सधर्माणस् तथा यायावरा गणाः । ऋषीणाम् उग्रतपसाम् धर्म-नैपुणदर्शिनाम् ॥ ) 12. 236 19 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 12. 244. 19: प्रत्यक्षः धर्मो धर्मफलं सत्यसङ्कल्पत्वा-दिकं येषां ते प्रत्यक्षधर्माणः). B. Their history: (1) Yāyāvaras were the forefathers of Jaratkāru; he once saw them hanging with their heads down and holding on to a bunch of grass; a mouse residing in a hole was slowly eating up that bunch of grass; Jaratkāru addressed them; he pitied their plight for they were without food, were lean, pitiable, affli-cted and waiting for help; he showed his readiness to help them by offering them the fourth, the third, the half, of his austerities, or even all of them; Yāyāvaras told him that they were falling down in the impure hell because of the non-continuation of their line (संतान-प्रक्षय); his austerities would not help them; they told him they were sages known as Yāyāvaras, they had fallen down from the holy world due to the discontinuation of their line (संतान-प्रक्षय); their austerities had come to an end; there was no one to continue their line; the only one, named Jaratkāru, was as good as nothing for this purpose; he was versed in the Vedas but had not married and had no progeny; hence they were hanging head down in the ditch; if ever the person to whom they were addressing met Jaratkāru he should tell him their plight, ask him to marry and beget progeny; the bunch of grass to which they were clinging was their only support; if they fell down along with their ancestors, Jaratkāru too would fall down into the hell; neither austerities, nor sacrifices, nor any thing else was equal to a child 1. 41. 3-30; 1. 13. 10-30; Jarat-kāru then disclosed his identity to Yāyā-varas and asked them to punish him; they told him that fortunately he had come there and asked him the reason of his not marrying; Jaratkāru told them that by ob-serving celibacy he wanted to take his body to the next world (ऊर्ध्वरेताः शरीरं वै प्रापयेयम् अमुत्र वै); however now that he had seen their plight he had decided to marry provided he found a maiden having his name and also if he was not required to support her (सनाम्नीं यद्य् अहं कन्याम् उपलप्स्ये कदाचन … न भरेयं च याम् अहम्); Jaratkāru did not get a maiden since he was old; dejected he went to the forest and addressed all beings, moving and not moving, and even those concealed, telling them that Yāyāvaras had asked him to marry and so he requested them to give him a maiden who bore his name and whom he was not required to support 1. 42. 1-15; when Jaratkāru's conditions were fulfilled, he married; when Āstīka was born, he saved Yāyāvaras and took off great burden of his ancestors; Jaratkāru went to heaven, along with his ancestors (पितॄंश् च तारयाम् आस संतत्या तपसा तथा । … अपहृत्य गुरुं भारम् पितॄणां … । जरत्कारुर् गतः स्वर्गं सहितः स्वैः पितामहैः ॥ ) 1. 13. 41-46; (2) Yāyāvaras mentioned among those who, after retiring to forest (during the वानप्रस्थाश्रम 12. 236. 4-5), went to heaven 12. 236. 18-19. C. Certain persons referred to in relation to Yāyāvaras; (1) Born in the family of Yāyāvaras; Āstīka (यायावरकुलोत्पन्न) 15. 43. 10; Jaratkāru (यायावरकुले … भविष्यति) 1. 34. 12; (2) Prominent among Yāyāvaras: Jaratkāru (यायावराणां … प्रवरः) 1. 13. 10.
यौधेय: Yaudheya m. (pl.): Name of a people. A. Description: Heroic (शूर) 7. 132. 25. B. Epic events: (1) Their Kṣatriya kings (राजन्याः 2. 48. 13; क्षत्रियाः 2. 48. 16) brought wealth by hundreds (आहार्षुः क्षत्रिया वित्तं शतशो … ) for the Rāja-sūya of Yudhiṣṭhira 2. 48. 13, 16; (2) On the eleventh day of war, Arjuna affli-cted Yaudheya Kṣatriyas with arrows; but even though they were being killed by Arjuna they showered different kinds of arrows on Arjuna so that Arjuna, his chariot, and Kṛṣṇa became invisible as they were concealed by arrows; feeling that they had hit the target and Arjuna and Kṛṣṇa were killed, Yaudheyas and others roared, waived their upper garments and blew भेरिस्, horns and conches; Arjuna removed the screen of arrows by employing वायव्यास्त्र 7. 18. 16-22; (3) In the night war, Yudhiṣṭhira killed hordes of Yaudheyas and others; at that time the Yaudheya warriors shouted in confusion “kill him, bring him, capture him,” or “pierce him, cut him” (हताहरत गृह्णीत विध्यत व्यवकृन्तत । इत्य् आसित् तुमुलः शब्दो युधिष्ठिररथं प्रति ॥ ) 7. 132. 25-26; Arjuna too killed many Yaudheyas with arrows 7. 136. 5; (4) On the seven-teenth day, at night, when Dhṛtarāṣṭra asked Saṃjaya who in the army of Kaura-vas were dead and who were alive (8. 4. 3), Saṃjaya mentioned Yaudheyas among those who were killed by Arjuna 8. 4. 46.
यौन: Yauna m. (pl.): Name of a people. A. Location: They, along with Kām-bojas, Gāndhāras and others belonged to the Uttarāpatha (उत्तरापथजन्मानः) 12. 200. 40. B. Description: Sinful (पापकृत्); they roamed over the earth living like dogs, crows, बलस् and vultures; they did not exist in the Kṛta age but were to be found since the Tretā age; they did not believe in Bhūtapati being the superintendent of the people (एष भूत-पतिस् तात स्वध्यक्षश् च प्रकीर्तितः । निरध्यक्षांस् तु कौन्तेय कीर्तयिष्यामि तान् अपि ॥ ; यौनकाम्बोजगान्धाराः … । ।) 12. 200. 38, 40; (for other citations see Uttarāpatha); according to Bhīṣma all this information was declared by Nārada (देवदेवर्षिर् आचष्ट नारदः) 12. 200. 44.
